failure_summary.description: The agent selected stronger quantitative or scope claims than the theorem or evidence established.
The agent misread endpoint, orientation, or origin-count conditions instead of following the stated hypotheses and definitions.
The agent failed to match the exact ordering of the MZV argument blocks to the choices.
The agent guessed a specialized dynamical theorem from analogy and asserted the wrong generic behavior.

patch.reasoning: The skill already contains topic-specific warnings for several of these errors. A prominent option-audit step can make those distinctions operational: verify every clause and modifier in a choice against the exact theorem, rather than accepting a plausible core statement or adding an unsupported refinement.

edits.target: Before choosing an option, identify the exact definition or theorem the question is testing. Parse every displayed expression literally, then compare the options’ hypotheses, quantifiers, exponents, endpoint spaces, and requested level of detail. Do not invent a theorem, exceptional case, or stronger conclusion from analogy or from a plausible-sounding citation. If you cannot verify a stronger claim, select only what the stated result supports.
edits.content: **Option-audit protocol:** Treat each choice as a conjunction and verify every clause against the exact theorem and prompt before selecting it. Added modifiers—such as “only when,” “even without,” an exact coefficient, uniqueness, or inclusion of an endpoint—are additional claims, not harmless wording; one unsupported clause makes the whole choice invalid. Do not rank choices by what seems most plausible or strongest: select only the strongest statement actually established, and do not infer specialized results from analogy or a single example.
